doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Leonard Feather's encyclopedia and friends in bebop
summary: Recollections of her father and Ira Gitler compiling the encyclopedia and his friendship with Charlie Parker.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah that was a gift for me, I think a high school graduation. And when I look at it now it’s really lovely to read and it’s quaint because he included addresses of people.

Right. I remember when he was putting that encyclopedia together he and Ira Gitler, it was this massive dining room table we had that my parents kept for decades. And all these biographies were strewn all over. It was quite an undertaking considering that these musicians were all over the world, some of them were not very good about getting back to him for one reason or another, and it’s really kind of amazing that he did it and got as much information as he did.

Yes and it’s informative to read now. What he chose to write about people back then, in the 60s, and we know them now from their whole career after that but we sometimes forget what they did when they were young men and women.

Yeah. Yeah well it’s so magical in a way, the way my dad arrived on the scene exactly when he did because everything was happening. And he was friends with Charlie Parker. I have — I’m staring across the room at my dad’s book Inside Bebop framed, and it’s autographed “To Leonard, my best friend, Charlie Parker.”
